headline: A study is a “reading room”, first attested in the late 800s.

sources.quote: First attested in the late 800s. Appears to be a borrowing from Middle Chinese 書齋 (MC syo tsreaj, “a reading room, a study”).

examples.ja: 彼は書斎にいる。
examples.en: He is in his library.

examples.ja: 私の書斎は２階にある。
examples.en: My study is upstairs.

meaning: to repeat, to do something over again
headline: To repeat is to “reel” and “return”.

morphemes.meaning: to reel, to wind, to spin

sources.quote: 繰り (kuri, 連用形 (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 繰る (kuru, “to reel, to wind, to spin”)) + 返す (kaesu, “to return”)

examples.ja: 歴史は繰り返す。
examples.en: History repeats itself.

examples.ja: 彼は質問を繰り返しました。
examples.en: He repeated his question.

headline: The piano is a clipped “pianoforte” — or a plain Italian word, depending on the source.

sources.quote: From Italian piano, possibly via English piano. Some sources derive this as a clipping of ピアノフォルテ (pianoforute, “pianoforte”), itself borrowed from Italian pianoforte.

examples.ja: 古いピアノだよ。
examples.en: It's an old piano.

examples.ja: ピアノは高いです。
examples.en: A piano is expensive.

headline: “News” ends in ス, not ズ — an English /z/ heard as an s.

sources.quote: Borrowed from English news. The English word-final voiced sound /z/ is sometimes transcribed as if it was voiceless, as ス (su), rather than as ズ (zu), especially if it represents English -s (plural suffix). Compare ゼット (zetto, “zed”). Also compare Korean 스 (seu) which is used along with 즈 (jeu).

examples.ja: ニュースがもれた。
examples.en: The news leaked out.

examples.ja: このニュースは初耳です。
examples.en: This news is new to me.

headline: A single month, ひとつき, may be an old “one month” — and Chinese-derived readings of the same spelling sit alongside it.

sources.quote: Possibly from Old Japanese.
Compound of 一 (hito, “one”) + 月 (tsuki, “month”).

headline: Saying “excuse me for disturbing you” is, word by word, an honorific, a “nuisance”, and “do”.

sources.quote: Compound of 御(お) (o-, honorific prefix) + 邪(じゃ)魔(ま) (jama, “nuisance, bother”) + します (shimasu, formal of する (suru), “to do”).

headline: An amateur is a “plain person” — and the “person” part is a form of 人 that never stands on its own.

sources.quote: Compound of 素(しろ) (shiro, “plain, undecorated”) + 人(うと) (-uto, “person”).

The term 人 (hito, “person”) appears in various older compounds with a root form of 人 (*puto → *buto → *udo, *puto → *futo → *uto). This form is never seen in isolation, and it often undergoes further phonetic changes to combine with preceding vowels. Compare the formation of 仲人 (nakōdo), from naka + udo; 旅人 (tabiudo), from tabi + udo.

examples.ja: 彼はしろうとの庭師だが、彼の育てる花は美しい。
examples.en: He is an amateur gardener, but his flowers are beautiful.

examples.ja: あのシロウト歌手は文句なくタレントショーで一位となった。
examples.en: The amateur singer won first in the talent show hands down.
furigana: なくタレントショーで

headline: “By oneself” began as “body” plus a possessive plus “quality”, and its ず is a softened つ.

sources.quote: ⟨mi₂ tu kara⟩ → */mʷɨdukara/ → /mid͡zukara/ → /mizukara/
Originally a compound of 身 (mi, “body”) + つ (tsu, Old Japanese possessive particle) + 柄 (kara, “quality, characteristic → by itself”).
The okurigana ら (ra) is used to indicate the reading.

examples.ja: 彼は自分自ら辞めた。
examples.en: He did so of his own accord.

examples.ja: 自らスパイと認める。
examples.en: Confess himself to be a spy.

headline: The bentō was probably a “face tub” — and the 弁 was picked to avoid another character's meaning.

sources.quote: /bentau/ → /bentɔː/ → /bentoː/.

Probably a variant of 面(めん)筒(とう) (mentō, “(obsolete) tub for distributing portions of food”), from 面(めん) (men, “face”) + 筒(とう) (tō, “bucket, tub”) (originally referring to a tub for washing the face), both from Middle Chinese.
The use of 弁 for ben is an example of phonetic ateji (当(あ)て字(じ)), due to 便 having another sense of “human excrement”.
Shift from 弁(べん)当(とう) (bentō) above, shortening the vowel.

examples.ja: 駅で弁当を買った。
examples.en: I bought a box lunch at the station.

examples.ja: 暖かい弁当が買える。
examples.en: We can buy hot lunches.

headline: “Flashy” may come from a lively “breaking melody” on the shamisen — the 派 is only ateji.

sources.quote: Probably from 破手 (hade, “breaking melody”, in reference to a lively style of samisen playing), or possibly a shift from haede, as a compound of 映え (hae, “shining; glory”, the 連用形 (ren'yōkei, “continuative or stem form”) of verb 映える (haeru, “to shine; to be glorious, to be outstanding”)) + 手 (te, “hand; style, way, state”). The te changes to de as an instance of rendaku (連濁).
Appears from the late 1600s.
The use of the 派 character is an example of ateji (当(あ)て字(じ)).

examples.ja: これは派手すぎる。
examples.en: This is too bright.

examples.ja: このネクタイは派手すぎますよ。
examples.en: I'm afraid this tie is too loud.

headline: Asia comes through Dutch — and the kanji for it came from Chinese.

sources.quote: Probably from Dutch Azië.
Kanji form from Chinese 亞細亞 /亚细亚 (Yàxìyà)

headline: Coffee came by way of Dutch, with English leaning on it, from an Arabic word — and it has two twins.

sources.quote: Borrowing from Dutch koffie, also influenced by English coffee, ultimately from Arabic قَهْوَة (qahwa). Doublet of カフェ (kafe) and カフワ (kafuwa).

headline: A girl is a “female child” — with a second, rarer name built on another word for “woman”.

sources.quote: Compound of 女 (onna, “a woman; female”) + の (no, appositional particle) + 子 (ko, “a child”).

examples.ja: エミはよい女の子だ。
examples.en: Emi is a good girl.

examples.ja: 健は女の子に親切です。
examples.en: Ken is kind to the girls.

headline: A workplace mixes a Chinese-derived “job” with a native-sounding “place” — a clue that it was coined in Japan.

sources.quote: Given the mixed Sinitic-Japanese reading, probably coined in Japan as a compound of 職 (shoku, “employment, trade, job”, on'yomi, from Middle Chinese) + 場 (ba, “place, site”, kun'yomi, from Old Japanese).

examples.ja: 彼は職場でまだ仕事中だ。
examples.en: He is still at work in the workroom.

examples.ja: 職場に出てもいいですか。
examples.en: Can I go to work?

headline: The crescent moon is the “third-day moon”: a moon named for the third day of a lunar month.

morphemes.meaning: third day of a lunar month

sources.quote: From Old Japanese.
Compound of 三日 (mika, “third day of a lunar month”) + 月 (tsuki, “moon”). The tsuki changes to zuki as an instance of rendaku (連濁).

headline: Whereabouts is “the direction one goes” — and its last syllable is a worn-down he.

sources.quote: ⟨yukupe₁⟩ → */jukupʲe/ → /jukuɸe/ → /jukuwe/ → /jukue/
From Old Japanese.
From verb 行く (yuku, “to go”) + 辺 (-he, “direction, location”).

examples.ja: 杳として行方が知れない。
examples.en: Nothing whatever is known of him.

examples.ja: 彼の行方は誰にもわからない。
examples.en: God knows where he has gone.

headline: A museum is a “building of wide learning”.

sources.quote: 博物 (hakubutsu, “wide learning”) + 館 (kan, “building”)

examples.ja: 我々は博物館へ行った。
examples.en: We went to the museum.

examples.ja: 博物館はどこにありますか。
examples.en: Where is the museum?

headline: A lost child is a “wandering child” — with the middle syllable worn away.

sources.quote: Alteration of 迷い子 (mayoigo). The ko changes to go as an instance of rendaku (連濁).

examples.ja: 彼らはみんなで迷子を探した。
examples.en: They all sought for the lost child.

examples.ja: 村人たちは迷子を捜しに出た。
examples.en: The villagers went in search of the missing child.

pos: noun or participle which takes the aux. verb suru
nouns which may take the genitive case particle 'no'
headline: Sleeping in is, word for word, a “sleeping boy”.

sources.quote: Compound of 寝 (ne, “sleeping”, the 連用形 (ren'yōkei, “the continuative or stem form”) of verb 寝る (neru, “to sleep”)) + 坊 (bō, “boy”, term of endearment).

examples.ja: 彼はときどき寝坊する。
examples.en: He sometimes sleeps in.

examples.ja: 僕は寝坊して学校に遅刻した。
examples.en: I overslept and was late for school.

headline: “Gram” was once ガラム — like ガラス and グラス, before it settled.

sources.quote: Borrowed from French gramme or English gramme, gram. Original form was ガラム (garamu) (compare to ガラス (garasu) and グラス (gurasu)).

headline: “Unskilled” may be “at the edge” of what you can do.

sources.quote: Probably a semantic shift from 端 (heta, “edge of something”), referring metaphorically to the edge of one's abilities or knowledge.
The kanji spelling appears to be an instance of jukujikun (熟(じゅく)字(じ)訓(くん)).

examples.ja: 彼は字が下手だ。
examples.en: His handwriting is poor.

examples.ja: 彼は運転が下手だ。
examples.en: He is a bad driver.

pos: noun or participle which takes the aux. verb suru
headline: Gymnastics got its name in the early Meiji school reforms, when physical education joined the curriculum.

sources.quote: Apparently coined in Japanese from Middle Chinese-derived elements, as a compound of 体 (tai, “body”) + 操 (sō, “control, manipulate”). First cited in education-related materials from the early Meiji Period in the early 1870s, as part of educational reforms that included the addition of physical education to school curricula.

examples.ja: 彼は体操が得意だ。
examples.en: He is good at gymnastics.

examples.ja: 健康のために体操する。
examples.en: I take exercise for health.

headline: Fur is “hair-skin” — with a Chinese-derived twin of the same spelling attested centuries earlier.

sources.quote: Compound of 毛 (ke, “fur, body hair”) + 皮 (kawa, “skin, pelt”). The kawa changes to gawa as an instance of rendaku (連濁).

First cited to a work from 1690, but possibly older, considering the mid-1200s appearance of Chinese-derived homograph 毛皮 (mōhi). This kegawa reading appears to have mostly superseded the mōhi reading.

headline: A razor is “hair-shaver” — and the kanji came ready-made from Chinese.

sources.quote: Compound of 髪 (kami, “hair on the head”) + 剃り (sori, “shaving facial hair or body hair; a shaver”, the 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 剃(そ)る (soru, “to shave facial hair or body hair”).). First cited in the ten-volume Wamyō Ruijushō of 934 CE.
The kanji are from Chinese 剃刀 (tìdāo).

headline: “Citizen” came from Chinese — but a native “country” and “people” compound hides behind the same spelling.

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese compound 國民 (MC kwok mjin).

examples.ja: 日本人は勤勉な国民だ。
examples.en: The Japanese are an industrious people.

examples.ja: 国民は重税に苦しんだ。
examples.en: The people groaned under the burden of heavy taxation.

headline: A crowd is “people” who are “full”.

morphemes.meaning: to go into, be full of, have a lot of

sources.quote: Compound of 人(ひと) (hito, “person”) + 込(こ)み (komi, 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 込(こ)む (komu, “to go into, be full of, have a lot of”).).

examples.ja: 人込みの中で彼とあった。
examples.en: I met him in the crowd.

examples.ja: 彼は人ごみでスリにあった。
examples.en: He had his pocket picked in the crowd.

meaning: (someone else's) house; home -- polite word for 家 (いえ) --
headline: Politely “your home” mixes a native honorific with a Chinese-derived word for “home”.

sources.quote: Compound of 御 (o-, honorific prefix, kun'yomi) + 宅 (taku, “home”, on'yomi).

examples.ja: 明日お宅に伺います。
examples.en: I'll call at your house tomorrow.

examples.ja: お宅の犬は大きいですね。
examples.en: Your dog is very big.

headline: A bus, a bath and a bass all hide in one two-syllable word.

sources.quote: Borrowed from English bus.
Borrowed from English bath.
Borrowed from English bass.
Borrowed from German Bass.

examples.ja: バス通学と積極的差別是正措置などが論争の多い話題だった。
examples.en: School busing and taking a proactive stance against discrimination were hotly debated topics.

headline: Hiragana is “smooth kana”, with かな voiced to がな.

sources.quote: Compound of 平 (hira, “flat, smooth”) + 仮名 (kana). The kana changes to gana as an instance of rendaku (連濁).

headline: A policy is literally a “direction needle” — another name for a magnetic needle.

sources.quote: 方 (“direction”) + 針 (“needle”), another name for the 磁針 (jishin, “magnetic needle”), with the meaning figuratively extending to "guidance" in general.

examples.ja: 彼らは新方針を採用した。
examples.en: They adopted a new policy.

examples.ja: 自己の方針をあくまで守れ。
examples.en: Keep to your own line.

meaning: to be conspicuous, to stand out
headline: To stand out is, quite literally, for the “eye” to “stand”.

sources.quote: 目(め) (me, “eye”) + 立(た)つ (tatsu, “to stand”).
The tatsu changes to datsu as an instance of rendaku (連濁).

examples.ja: 林に竹が目立つ。
examples.en: Bamboo stands out in the woods.

examples.ja: 彼の額の傷は目立つ。
examples.en: The scar on his forehead is conspicuous.
